MODEL AND THE DESIGN THAT ANSWERS IT.         Every target this contract calls is third-party code that must be assumed hostile, and         `execute` is permissionless (deliberately: anyone willing to pay gas to enrich the         beneficiary is welcome \u2014 that is a feature, not a hole). Safety here comes from removing         capabilities rather than guarding them:         1. NO OWNER, NO ADMIN, NO UPGRADE PATH, NO SELFDESTRUCT. There is no privileged key to            steal, lose, or phish. What is deployed is what runs, forever.         2. IMMUTABLE BENEFICIARY. Value can only ever leave this contract toward one address fixed            at construction. A malicious caller's best available attack is to enrich ZERO.         3. NO DELEGATECALL, ANYWHERE. A delegatecall to hostile code would hand it this contract's            identity and storage. The opcode never appears; only CALL is used.         4. NO ETH VALUE SENDS. `Call` has no value field. Because the contract can never be made to            send ETH to an arbitrary address, ETH sitting here transiently cannot be redirected.         5. CONSERVATION INVARIANT. Whatever this contract holds when `execute` begins must still be            here (or already at the beneficiary) when it ends. This is what stops a caller from            passing `target=USDC, data=transfer(attacker,...)` to strip dust that arrived between            transactions. Checked for ETH and for every declared sweep token.         6. PROFIT INVARIANT. If the beneficiary's ETH gain is below `minProfitWei`, the whole            transaction reverts \u2014 the relay slot is not spent on a batch that does not pay.         7. RETURNDATA-BOMB DEFENSE. Calls are made in assembly with outsize=0, so a target returning            megabytes cannot inflate this contract's memory cost. Return data is never copied.         8. GAS-GRIEFING DEFENSE. Every call carries an explicit gas cap, and a reserve is held back            so the sweeps and invariant checks always complete.         9. REENTRANCY GUARD on `execute`, so profit accounting cannot be confused by a target that            calls back in.         WHAT THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT DO: it does not decide what to call. Target selection stays         off-chain in ZERO's discovery layer, where it can be simulated for free. `eth_call` on         `execute` is the simulation and it runs the identical code path, so what is simulated is         exactly what executes \u2014 no drift between the checker and the checked.","kind":"dev","methods":{"execute((address,uint32,bytes)[],address[],uint256)":{"params":{"calls":"the batch; a reverting entry is recorded and skipped, never fatal","minProfitWei":"revert the whole transaction unless the beneficiary gained at least this                     much ETH; pass 0 for best-effort mode (discovery), non-zero in production                     so a relay slot is never spent on an unprofitable batch","sweepTokens":"ERC20s to move to the beneficiary afterwards (may be empty)"},"returns":{"ethProfit":"  ETH the beneficiary gained across this transaction","succeeded":"  number of calls that returned successfully","successBits":"bit i set when calls[i] succeeded"}}},"stateVariables":{"_lock":{"details":"Reentrancy flag. 1 = idle, 2 = executing (non-zero to non-zero is the cheap transition)."}},"title":"ZeroHarvester \u2014 batched, failure-isolated, profit-gated caller for permissionless bounties.","version":1},"userdoc":{"events":{"Batch(address,uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256)":{"notice":"One event per batch. `successBits` bit i is set when calls[i] returned successfully;         ZERO reads this to learn which targets actually pay and prune the ones that never do."},"Swept(address,uint256)":{"notice":"Emitted whenever value is pushed to the beneficiary (token == address(0) means ETH)."}},"kind":"user","methods":{"BENEFICIARY()":{"notice":"The single address any value may ever reach. params.calls: the batch; a reverting entry is recorded and skipped, never fatal
params.minProfitWei: revert the whole transaction unless the beneficiary gained at least this                     much ETH; pass 0 for best-effort mode (discovery), non-zero in production                     so a relay slot is never spent on an unprofitable batch
params.sweepTokens: ERC20s to move to the beneficiary afterwards (may be empty)

returns.ethProfit: ETH the beneficiary gained across this transaction
returns.succeeded: number of calls that returned successfully
returns.successBits: bit i set when calls[i] succeeded

BENEFICIARY().notice: The single address any value may ever reach. Immutable, set once, at construction.

GAS_RESERVE().notice: Gas held back from the final call so sweeps and invariant checks cannot be starved.

MAX_CALLS().notice: Upper bound on batch size. 256 is not arbitrary: the result bitmap is one uint256, so         every outcome in a maximal batch fits in a single word of event data.

execute((address,uint32,bytes)[],address.notice: Run a batch of bounty calls, isolating failures, then sweep everything to the         beneficiary and require the batch actually paid.

rescueETH().notice: Push stray ETH to the beneficiary. Permissionless on purpose — there is no owner to         call it, and it has exactly one possible destination, so opening it to everyone costs         nothing and guarantees value can never be stranded here.

rescueToken(address).notice: Push a stray ERC20 to the beneficiary. Same reasoning as {rescueETH}.
